source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A program whose supporting research evidence is generally considered fairly weak or poorly established at present","B":"Medication management as its main focus, with fairly little emphasis placed on lifestyle change itself","C":"Cutting out essentially all carbohydrate-containing foods as the program's primary recommended strategy","D":"Modest weight loss and increased physical activity, shown to significantly reduce progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes"}}
source_row.rationale: Evidence-based diabetes prevention lifestyle programs typically focus on modest weight loss (often around 5-7% of body weight) and increased physical activity, shown in landmark research to significantly reduce progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.
